## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 2, titled *Sambādhaloma* (“Removing pubic hair”), is an expiation rule governing Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunī*s) in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a nun who removes hair from her groin or armpits commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Horner]. In the canonical analysis, the term *sambādha* is specifically defined as the armpits and the private parts [Horner]. As examined by Ute Hüsken, the introductory account (*vatthu*, Vin IV 260) targets the practice of removing or shaving pubic hair (*sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpeti*)—likened to the behavior of laywomen—rather than naked bathing, which is regulated separately under Pācittiya 21 [Hüsken 1997].

Parallel provisions forbidding the removal of pubic and body hair are found throughout other early monastic codes, confirming its wide transmission [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records resembling parallels across the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, as well as the Dharmaguptaka (Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 71), Sarvāstivāda (Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 73), Mahīśāsaka (Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 74 and Pc 180), and Mūlasarvāstivāda (Tibetan xct-mu-bi-vb-pc97; Chinese Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 74) traditions [SuttaCentral]. Although DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches meeting its similarity threshold, it identifies 223 internal Pali text-reuse matches across 76 Vinaya passages, reflecting standard legal phrasing shared prominently with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya rules 87, 84, 89, 85, 86, and 88 [DharmaNexus]. Modern English translations of the rule include those by I.B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner; SuttaCentral].
